acceptance.output_evidence: HOW MUCH USABLE HISTORY. DynamoDB opal-news-trending-daily -- the dated evidence of record -- runs 2025-11-21 to 2026-09-10: a 294-day calendar span with 289 days PRESENT and 5 ABSENT, 5,156 items, 2 to 26 per day. The five absent days are named rather than averaged away: 2025-11-23 (1), 2025-12-08..09 (2), 2025-12-31..2026-01-01 (2); two of the three runs straddle a holiday. Recent density is 599 items across 30 of the last 30 days. The S3 prefilter archive runs 2025-12-01 to 2026-09-10, 695 dated objects across 277 days. AGAINST THE BRIEF'S 'almost a full year': 294 calendar days is 9.7 months, 80% of a year, so the request is SUBSTANTIALLY MET AND NOT MET IN FULL, and the shortfall is at the OLD end -- there is nothing anywhere before 2025-11-21, so a window opening earlier gets MISSING HISTORY with these bounds rather than a thin answer. A SECOND ASYMMETRY: the table reaches 10 days FURTHER BACK than the archive (2025-11-21 vs 2025-12-01), so the two carriers are not interchangeable at the boundary and a cell that reached for the archive because it is easier to list would silently lose those days.  IS THE PREFILTER ARCHIVE THE FINAL TOPIC CLOUD? NO -- AND THE FINAL ONE HAS NO HISTORY AT ALL. Three reads decided it. (1) The archive carries the PRE-FILTER set: save_report_to_s3 writes report['trending_topics'], which is the top TOP_N_TOPICS = 100 detected keywords (news_trending_analysis/lambda_function.py:75, :594, :1186). (2) The final Topic Cloud is a DIFFERENT, SMALLER, FURTHER-FILTERED set: in the same function, balanced_topics = select_balanced_keywords(report['trending_topics'], total_keywords=50) runs AFTER the archive write and is then put through a sports-keyword filter before being written to s3://opal-data-portal-v2/json/sentiment/keyword-sentiments.json (:1405, the _TOPICCLOUD_SPORTS_KEYWORDS block, :1522-1527), and the consumer confirms the arrow -- keyword_drilldown_generator/lambda_function.py:9 and :108 read that exact key as 'the TopicCloud source file'. (3) THAT FINAL FILE HAS NO DATED ARCHIVE: list-objects-v2 over s3://opal-data-portal-v2/json/sentiment/ returns 722 keys of which EXACTLY 2 are top-level files (keyword-sentiments.json and fear-greed-index.json); the other 720 are keyword-history-articles/ (360) and keyword-history-summary/ (360), keyed by KEYWORD and not by date. There is ONE Topic Cloud object and it is overwritten in place. So the order's condition -- use the prefilter archive as the final historical Topic Cloud only after proof that it is -- fails, and the harder finding is that a historical Topic Cloud does not exist in the estate at all. The archive is used here as a CORROBORATOR only, with its own caveat printed: its object PATH date is the writer's naive local clock (news_trending_analysis:1366).  WHERE A READER WOULD STILL READ CAUSATION. Four places, none of which a sentence-level validator can reach. (i) ADJACENCY IS AN ARGUMENT -- putting a market moment and a headline in one sentence is the claim, whatever the verb is, and the closing disclaimer is a sentence competing with a layout. (ii) THE EVIDENCE IS SELECTED BY THE EVENT, so the set is not neutral: a 7-day lookback anchored on the event date means a reader sees topic-and-drawdown together every time and NEVER sees the quiet-window negative case that would falsify the causal reading; a control panel of topics from a quiet window would be the cheapest honest counterweight and is not in this order. (iii) RANK IS READ AS RELEVANCE -- topic_rank values like bearish-1 order the list, so the first topic beside a drawdown reads as the most RELATED when it is the most TRENDING, and nothing in the packet distinguishes the two. (iv) THE VALIDATOR'S DOMAIN IS DECLARED, NOT EXHAUSTIVE -- 18 regexes, and prose.py says so in its own comment; a model-written paragraph would find the uncovered member ('amid', 'as X slid', 'against a backdrop of') and pass. It binds today only because the generator is a template with no causal slot; on the day a model writes the prose the validator alone is NOT sufficient, and that is a decision to take deliberately rather than discover.
